I made these after being inspired by a v/traditionalwives post. As commented in traditional wives I am male, so participating there feels weird but they are the only place that talks about nutrition and food. I am going to try and help change that, so here is how you make fermented ginger carrots, along with a couple pictures...

{Recipe}

(Ingredients)

2 lbs carrots

1 tbsp minced ginger, more if you really like ginger

2 tbsp salt

2 or 3 tbsp of olive oil

(Tools and dishes needed)

1 large bowl

1 wooden spoon

1 quart mason jar

optional

1 something to smash with - you can just use the wooden spoon

1) Grate your carrots and mince your ginger into a large bowl with a cheese grater. I peeled my carrots first but you likely don't actually need to, and obviously you do need to peel the ginger.

2) Add 2 tablespoons of good salt, don't use shitty salt for this you are going to want something like redmonds kosher mineral salt. I fucking hate using jewish terms but in some cases you have to. Fuck those damned kikes...

3) Use something to smash the carrots down into the bowl for at least 15 minutes. I used a wooden spoon. You could use a potato masher or something, but I didn't want to because my potato masher feels weak to me and 15 minutes of smashing might be too much for it. The point of this step is you are trying to get juice out of the carrots. It takes a lot longer than you think and this step is absolutely crucial, the most important step. It is fine to take breaks while you are doing this, in fact breaks will actually help the salt extract more juices from the carrots. Smashing is necessary though, and it takes around 15 minutes of solid smashing.

4) Transfer everything into a jar, try to mostly just get the solid carrot matter at first, and tamp it down into the jar with a wooden spoon as you go. You need to pack it into the jar as firmly as possible, and you don't want any air bubbles which is why you tamp it down. Pour in the juice when finished.

5) The carrots must be underneath the juices, this is very important. There are a few methods of making this happen. You can use a whole cabbage leaf, and use it to wedge the carrots underneath the juices. The recipe I used at first, used the cabbage leaf method and it looked quite difficult to do on the video. I found another one that I am going to link at the end of this where the woman used the cabbage leaf method without much issue, however I read the comments on the video and found what I consider a better method. Put a thin layer of olive oil on top, nothing will float through the olive oil layer. I just used a spoon and put it at the top of the liquid, and poured olive oil onto the spoon for a layer of olive oil and it worked perfectly.

6) Do NOT seal the jars. You can put a lid on but don't use the metal lids with rubber seals. You can use the plastic storage lids for mason jars because they are not air tight. I just used a metal lid ring but didn't use the actual metal lid, instead I just used paper towel and used that as the lid with the metal ring. Then put the jars in the pantry if you have one, you want to keep them about room temp or a little cooler but not in the fridge that is too cold. Leave them for 4 days or so, until the bubbles stop.

7) Remove the layer of olive oil. I kept the oil and cooked some chicken with it later on. They should smell pretty awesome now and shouldn't lose much color or anything like that. You can remove the cabbage leaf and you are good to start eating some fermented ginger carrots. I am on my 4th batch now.

Something to note is this is how you make this recipe the first time only and this first time you make it is going to be very salty. The 2nd time you make it, use only 1 tbsp of salt instead of 2, and use the brine from the last batch. The carrots will be less salty the 2nd and 3rd time you make this recipe and is in my opinion best after the 3rd or so time. The first time you can use the carrots on top of rice and stuff like that to help even out the salt taste if it's too much for you. I will also note that this is almost identical to making sauerkraut but I'll make a new post about that to help fill the subverse up a little later on.

{recipe}

(Ingredients)

1 head of cabbage

2 tbsp salt

(Tools)

1 Large bowl

1 Quart mason jar

1 Something to smash with like a wooden spoon

1) Wash the cabbage and remove a full leaf without ripping it too much

2) Shred or chop the cabbage, I quartered the cabbage and used a mandolin slicer

3) Add the cabbage and salt to the large bowl and mix it around

4) Smash it for 10 or so minutes with the spoon

5) Add solid cabbage to the mason jar first, tamping down into the jar with wooden spoon to remove air bubbles and pack tightly. Then pour liquid over top

6) The cabbage must stay under the liquid, use the full cabbage leaf from step 1 to wedge everything in so its underneath the liquid. Anything above the liquid will very likely mold. The mold won't kill you, and you can just remove it and still eat the sauerkraut but if you just take care to make sure everything stays under the liquid you won't get any mold.
